import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.60

by V. P. Shunkov

Do there exist infinite finitely generated simple periodic (conjugacy)
biprimitively finite groups which contain both involutions and non-trivial
elements of odd order?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.60»

/-- A group is biprimitively finite if, for every finite subgroup $H$, any two
elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Subgroup G), Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group is conjugacy biprimitively finite if, for every finite subgroup
$H$, any two conjugate elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite
subgroup. -/
def IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Subgroup G), Finite H →
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      IsConj x y → (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime →
        Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/--
Do there exist infinite finitely generated simple periodic biprimitively finite
groups which contain both an involution and a non-trivial element of odd order?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.60» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsSimpleGroup G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧
      IsBiprimitivelyFinite G ∧
      (∃ x : G, orderOf x = 2) ∧
      (∃ y : G, y ≠ 1 ∧ Odd (orderOf y)) := by
  sorry

/--
Do there exist infinite finitely generated simple periodic conjugacy
biprimitively finite groups which contain both an involution and a non-trivial
element of odd order?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.60».variants.conjugacy : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsSimpleGroup G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧
      IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite G ∧
      (∃ x : G, orderOf x = 2) ∧
      (∃ y : G, y ≠ 1 ∧ Odd (orderOf y)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.60»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.60

by V. P. Shunkov

Do there exist infinite finitely generated simple periodic (conjugacy)
biprimitively finite groups which contain both involutions and non-trivial
elements of odd order?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.60»

/-- A group $G$ is biprimitively finite if, for every finite subgroup $H$ of
$G$, any two elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a finite subgroup. -/
def IsBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Subgroup G), Finite H →
    letI : (H.subgroupOf H.normalizer).Normal := Subgroup.normal_in_normalizer
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime → Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- A group $G$ is conjugacy biprimitively finite if, for every finite subgroup
$H$ of $G$, any two conjugate elements of prime order in $N_G(H)/H$ generate a
finite subgroup. -/
def IsConjugacyBiprimitivelyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Subgroup G), Finite H →
    letI : (H.subgroupOf H.normalizer).Normal := Subgroup.normal_in_normalizer
    ∀ x y : H.normalizer ⧸ H.subgroupOf H.normalizer,
      IsConj x y → (orderOf x).Prime → (orderOf y).Prime →
        Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/--
Do there exist infinite finitely generated simple periodic biprimitively finite
groups which contain both an involution and a non-trivial element of odd order?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.60» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G),
      Infinite G ∧ Group.FG G ∧ IsSimpleGroup G ∧ Monoid.IsTorsion G ∧
      IsBiprimitivelyFinite G ∧
      (∃ x : G, orderOf x = 2) ∧ (∃ y : G, y ≠ 1 ∧ Odd (orderOf y)) := by
  sorry
